source.title: Assessing Generalization Capability of 3D Semantic Segmentation Algorithms using 3D Point Clouds of Cultural Heritage
source.authors: T. Betsas; Hlias Tsarpalis; Andreas Georgopoulos

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; some table text is flattened, but the discussion states the principal test mIoU results explicitly.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates generalization of several 3D segmentation architectures on an unseen cultural-heritage scene, a new task and data setting for the catalog claim.
record.gate_note: The study measures performance on natural labels and reports validation-to-test differences for three models. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, fully connected versus convolutional image models, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or example removal. Other architecture performance values in Tables 5–9 are not extracted where the flattened layout does not clearly assign values to models.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out-scene performance of 3D point-cloud segmentation models. None of its experiments measures the specific relationships in V1–V8. A new generalization setting alone does not constitute a test of these versions; citations to Zhang and Neyshabur provide introductory context.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: PTv1 performs best among the tested recent models on the unseen ArCH scene. The authors propose a possible association between architecture and generalization, while requiring systematic hyperparameter optimization and broader architectural exploration before drawing definitive conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates 3D point-cloud semantic-segmentation architectures on cultural-heritage scenes, rather than testing the original studies' random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or generalization-measure methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation-to-test mIoU drop differs by architecture: PTv1 -3.5%, PTv2 -16.1%, and OACNNs -6.9%.

fits_no_version.finding: PTv1, PTv2 and OACNNs obtain discussion-reported test mIoU values of 61.3%, 21.4% and 25.9%, with validation-to-test decreases of 3.5, 16.1 and 6.9 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested ArCH recipes, PTv1 achieves higher unseen-scene mIoU and a smaller validation-to-test decrease than PTv2 and OACNNs. Architecture, training and augmentation differences prevent attributing the advantage solely to architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: The discussion reports higher validation than training loss across the experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested point-cloud segmentation models exhibit a training–validation loss gap on this ArCH setup.

record.peer_reviewed: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
record.problems: Only one held-out test scene was used. The authors note limited computational resources, point-cloud cropping that may hinder global-feature extraction, and no exhaustive fine-tuning; they call for systematic hyperparameter optimization and broader architectural exploration. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 5–9 contain additional overall and per-class metrics, but the supplied flattened table text does not consistently support assigning every value to a particular model and metric. Prior-work DGCNN results are not this study's own experiments.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets; optimizer differences across these architectures do not isolate this relationship.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Held-out performance with versus without network dropout; the listed RandomDropout data augmentation supplies no such comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Memorization-based example removal versus equally sized random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Additional segmentation metrics and inference-time comparisons do not supply a missing test of V1–V8. The paper inconsistently names the validation scene B SMV and SMG B.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No fully connected image-network comparison or test of local connectivity.
Optimizers differ across architectures, but optimizer effects are not isolated or compared.
Batch sizes differ across architectures, but batch-size effects are not isolated or compared.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
